constraint_decided_it: P50's actual condition -- 'This property is a shortcut for the more detailed path from E18 Physical Thing through P30i custody transferred through, E10 Transfer of Custody, P29 custody received by to E39 Actor, if and only if the custody has not been surrendered by the receiving actor at any later time' -- plus its FOL, which is an entailment FROM the path (P50(x,y) <= (Ex z)[E10(z) & P30i(x,z) & P29(z,y)] & not(Ex w)[... P28(w,y) & P182(z,w)]). B claims P50 is 'applicable when custody has not been separately tracked' and stands in for the path 'precisely when the intervening custodians are NOT separately recorded'; neither the scope note nor the FOL says that, and the FOL says the opposite (recording the events entails P50 rather than excluding it). A instead relies on Introduction > Applied Form > Shortcuts, whose stated asymmetry ('An instance of the fully-articulated path always implies an instance of the shortcut property. However ... an instance of the fully-articulated path cannot always be inferred from an instance of the shortcut property') is exactly the constraint that decides the case, and on Modelling principles > Monotonicity, whose fourth consequence says 'If a more specific temporal knowledge is required/available, it is recommended to explicitly describe the events leading to the assertion of that property for that item.'
better_modelling: Three instances of E10 Transfer of Custody, each P30 transferred custody of the ledgers (E22 Human-Made Object, a subclass of E18 so within P30's declared range), P28 custody surrendered by / P29 custody received by the outgoing and incoming E39 Actor, and -- the piece both answers omit -- each E10 P4 has time-span an E52 Time-Span carrying 1934 / 1988 / 2010, without which the chain is not orderable and the Monotonicity argument for using events instead of 'current' properties is not actually cashed out. Each signed handover note is an E31 Document that P70 documents (domain E31, range E1) the corresponding E10, as A has it. The 2010 'formal donation' additionally warrants an E8 Acquisition with P23 transferred title from the county record office and P22 transferred title to the archive if title passed, since E8's and E10's scope notes both state that 'The CIDOC CRM therefore models legal ownership (E8 Acquisition) and physical custody (E10 Transfer of Custody) separately' and that institutions model accession as combinations of the two -- B flags this, A wrongly rejects E8 across all three moves. P49/P50 stay assertable as derived summaries entailed by the path, not as alternatives to it.
reasoning: Both reach the same core modelling and both apply P28/P29/P30 within their declared domain E10 and ranges E39/E18, so neither is wrong on domain-range grounds. A is suboptimal: it rejects E8 Acquisition for the 2010 donation even though E10's own scope note declares ownership and custody separately modelled and combined for accession, and it omits P4 has time-span / E52 for the three dates; its label 'E19/E22 Physical Thing' is also a slip (E18 is Physical Thing) though both classes fall inside P30's range. B is unsupported: its load-bearing justification attributes to P50's scope note and FOL a condition about custody 'not being separately tracked' that neither text contains -- P50's real qualifier is 'if and only if the custody has not been surrendered by the receiving actor at any later time', and t1632 shows the SIG reading these FOLs as inferences from recorded events -- and it separately miscounts the case as 'four moves'. A's remaining citations verify: E10's scope note does say the physical-versus-legal split 'should be expressed using the property P2 has type', and t1394 is the Issue 475 e-vote that introduced exactly that wording; B's t1469 (Getty Mrs Fitzherbert provenance HW for issue 516) also verifies.
